summary: cfgzen ships a Windows-only native binary that performs host fingerprinting and sandbox evasion at import time
details: The package's __init__.py unconditionally invokes `_native.platform_check()` from a shipped Windows-only `_native.pyd` (Rust/PyO3, ~295 KB) on `import dotcfg`. The binary embeds host-identity environment variable names (COMPUTERNAME, HOSTNAME, USERNAME, USER, LOCALAPPDATA, TEMP), a hardcoded browser User-Agent string (`Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64) AppleWebKit/537.36`) and HTTP `GET` method, a CI/sandbox detection list (GITHUB_ACTIONS, GITLAB_CI, JENKINS_HOME, TRAVIS, CIRCLECI, CODEBUILD_BUILD_ID, TF_BUILD, BUILDKITE, DRONE, APPVEYOR, CI, CONTINUOUS_INTEGRATION, TEAMCITY_VERSION, HEROKU_TEST_RUN_ID) used to remain dormant in analysis environments, filenames masquerading as Microsoft components (`Microsoft\WindowsApps\RuntimeBroker_v2.exe`, `Microsoft\Edge\Temp\msedge_installer.exe`), a staging filename `envcorecache.dat`, and a reversed-string literal. The Python docstring frames the call as a benign `platform_check` / state prewarm, but none of these primitives — host-identity enumeration, browser User-Agent, HTTP client, CI-evasion gate, Microsoft-service masquerade filenames — are required by a configuration/.env file parser. Shape is host-fingerprint-then-beacon plus a dropper staging path, gated to fire on developer and production machines while staying quiet in CI.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
